title: owo-lib issue #455: [1.21.1] DataResult is class loaded to early causing a crash

text:
[issue by benio1394]
Mc version: 1.21.1
Fabric: 0.18.2
Logs (there is no crash report): https://pastebin.com/t1SN82eY

[comment by Dragon-Seeker (member)]
`Caused by: org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.transformer.throwables.MixinTargetAlreadyLoadedException: Critical problem: owo.mixins.json:DataResultMixin from mod owo target com.mojang.serialization.DataResult was loaded too early.`

It seems that DataResult has been loaded in some way by a Mixin Plugin or something else by another mod, leading to an inability to apply a mixin. You will need to go through your mods to figure out the problem mod.

[comment by careybernstein (none)]
After receiving this same error running MC 1.21.11, Neoforge 21.11.42, and Oritech which requires owo, I tried a clean install with no other plugins installed except for the owo library, and still receiving the crash error.

[comment by ASC-kuro-code (none)]
We're hitting the same "loaded too early" issue on a dedicated NeoForge server (21.1.226, MC 1.21.1, Temurin 21.0.10) — tested all 12 NeoForge beta builds and every single one crashes.

It's not caused by another mod. NeoForge itself loads `CompoundTag` and `ComponentSerialization` early via `ImmediateWindowHandler$DummyProvider.updateModuleReads()` → `Class.forName()` during game layer acceptance, before the mixin subsystem processes any configs. This happens with owo-lib as the only mod installed.

The affected mixins are:
- `NbtCompoundMixin` → `net.minecraft.nbt.CompoundTag`
- `text.TextCodecsMixin` → `net.minecraft.network.chat.ComponentSerialization`

Additionally, the **accessories** mod has its own `temp_fixes.NbtCompoundMixin` targeting `CompoundTag` with the same crash.

This blocks the entire owo → accessories → mega evolution chain on NeoForge dedicated servers (Mega Showdown, ZA Megas, Horret's Extended Megas, Starlight Fusion).

Marking this wontfix means owo-lib's NeoForge port is unusable on dedicated servers. The root cause is in NeoForge's bootstrap, but the fix would need to come from owo-lib by either not mixing into these early-loaded classes or finding an alternative approach.
